entries.title: 2 Chronicles 23:1
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
1 Jehoiada, having set things in order, makes Joash king. 12 Athaliah is slain. 16 Jehoiada restores the worship of God.

seventh year. 2Ki 11:4-16 covenant with him. 15:12; 1Sa 18:3; Ne 9:38

entries.title: 2 Chronicles 23:2
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
went about. Ps 112:5; Mt 10:16; Eph 5:15 the chief of.Houbigant omits the words of Israel. Bp. Patrick, however, is of the opinion that Judah is here called by the general name of Israel: but it is probable, that these "chief fathers of Israel," were the descendants of those priests and Levites, and other pious persons of the ten tribes, who left their cities and possessions, and joined themselves to Judah, in the days of Jeroboam. See the parallel passages.

11:13-17; 1Ch 15:12; 24:6

entries.title: 2 Chronicles 23:5
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: the king's house. 2Ki 11:5,6; Eze 44:2,3; 46:2,3 the gate. Ac 3:2

entries.title: 2 Chronicles 23:9
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: spears. 1Sa 21:9; 2Sa 8:7 which were in the house.When the soldier retired from the tumults of war to the bosom of his family, he frequently hung up his arms in the temple, as a grateful acknowledgment of the protection he had received, and of the victories he had won. It is highly probable, therefore, that the arms of David which Jehoiada delivered to the captains of hundreds, "which were in the house of God," were laid up in the tabernacle by David when he resigned the command of his armies to his generals; and there is reason to believe that his conduct, in this respect, was followed by many of his companions in arms.

entries.title: 2 Chronicles 23:10
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: side of the temple. Heb. shoulder of the house. 2Ki 11:11 along by. 6:12; Ex 40:6

entries.title: 2 Chronicles 23:13
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: she looked. Ps 14:5 the king. 34:31; 2Ki 23:3 and the princes. Nu 10:1-10; 1Ch 15:24 all the people. 1Ki 1:39,40; 1Ch 12:40; Pr 11:10; 29:2 sounded. Jud 7:8,18-22; 2Ki 9:13 the singers. 1Ch 15:16-22,27; 25:1-8 Then Athaliah. Ec 9:12 Treason. Heb. Conspiracy. 1Ki 18:17,18; 2Ki 9:23; Ro 2:1,2

entries.title: 2 Chronicles 23:14
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
Have her forth.The Vulgate has here, and in the parallel place, {Educite illam extra septa templi,} "Take her out beyond the precincts of the temple." These were walls erected in parallel lines, and forming an extensive range of buildings around the sacred edifice.

Ex 21:14 whoso followeth her.He who takes her part let him be instantly slain.

2Ki 10:25; 11:8,15 Slay her not. Eze 9:7

entries.title: 2 Chronicles 23:15
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content:
the horse gate.This gate was in the eastern wall of the city, towards the brook Kidron, (Jer 31:40,) at which the king's horses probably went out from the stables at Millo. It was near the temple; and some Rabbins suppose that, in order to go to the temple, a person might go on horseback to this place, but was then obliged to alight.

Ne 3:28 they slew her there. 22:10; Jud 1:7; Ps 5:6; 55:23; Mt 7:2; Jas 2:13; Re 16:5-7

entries.title: 2 Chronicles 23:17
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: the house of Baal. 34:4,7; 2Ki 10:25-28; 11:18; 18:4 brake his altars. De 12:3; Isa 2:18; Zec 13:2,3 slew Mattan. De 13:5,9; 1Ki 18:40; 2Ki 11:18,19

entries.title: 2 Chronicles 23:18
entries.author: R. A. Torrey (editor)
entries.content: whom David. 1Ch 23:1-24:31 as it is written. Nu 28:1-31 by David. Heb. by the hands of David. 29:25; 1Ch 25:1-31
